item.title: Terms
item.description:
The following terms are in use in this module and coming as much as possible from the official Hydro-Quebec electricy rates document (page 31) :

https://www.hydroquebec.com/data/documents-donnees/pdf/electricity-rates.pdf

and from the “Régie de l’énergie” document :

http://publicsde.regie-energie.qc.ca/projets/469/DocPrj/R-4057-2018-B-0062-DDR-RepDDR-2018_10_26.pdf#page=124

Period

In the context of the Winter Credits a period is a time window during which a specific billing or algorythmic logic is applied by Hydro-Quebec.

item.title: Optimization logics
item.description:
The following information is derived from the formulas from this “Régie de l’énergie” filing:

http://publicsde.regie-energie.qc.ca/projets/469/DocPrj/R-4057-2018-B-0062-DDR-RepDDR-2018_10_26.pdf#page=127

Overview

The winter credit program implement a set of calculations to estimate the real amount of energy you saved during a critical peak event. In short, they use the consumption from the five previous days of the same kind that did not have a critical event (five last weekdays or five last weekend days) to estimate a regular consumption.

item.title: Winter Credit Sensors
item.description:
Sensor description

The following entities are created for the DCPC (Winter Credits) rate. Peak event entities read their data from the dedicated calendar configured in the integration. For details about each period, see the optimization logic page.

Warning

Entities that represent the current state (Winter Credit Status, Critical Peak Active, Preheat Active) depend on the calendar events and the coordinator update. For automations that must run at a precise time, prefer the timestamp entities (Next Anchor Start, Next Peak Start, Next Preheat Start, etc.).
